summary: Backend-only verification of Kotiz corrections (Parties A, C-backend, H). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_kotiz_corrections.py with 10 pytest cases — ALL PASS (10/10). Verified: (A) /api/payments/my/year/:yearId and /api/exceptional/mine require auth, filter by userId=req.user.id, and return 404 for admin@delete-test.local (no member profile — expected); (Admin) /api/payments/year/:yearId and /api/exceptional remain admin-only (200 for admin, 401 without token); (H) DB-level lockout triggers after exactly 5 failed password attempts (403 with 'bloqué' message on 6th), a successful login via SuperAdmin password-reset unlocks the account, and the failed-attempts counter is reset to 0 after a successful login (next wrong pw → 401 not 403).

minor.issue: The IP-based express-rate-limit is set to max: 5 / 15 min AND max=5 corresponds exactly to the DB lockout threshold, which means legitimate users hitting 5 wrong passwords also get IP-throttled and cannot see the 403 'compte bloqué' message on the 6th attempt from the same IP — the message only surfaces from a *different* IP or after 15 min. Consider raising loginLimiter max to e.g. 10-15 so the DB lockout message is what actually surfaces first.

The IP loginLimiter uses the default in-memory store which is per-process. In multi-node/serverless deploys the 5/15-min budget is per-node, effectively multiplying attempts. Fine for single-node preview; document/consider a shared store (Redis) in production.

action_items: PARTIE C (web /payments crash) was NOT tested — request scope is 'backend only'. Main agent should verify manually on the Next.js web app that /payments loads without React error when the MemberPayment interface is used.
Consider bumping loginLimiter max from 5 to 10-15 so users encountering the DB-lockout 403 aren't shadowed by the generic IP rate-limit 429 (minor UX).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/payments.js line 34-47 (GET /my/year/:yearId): correct — filters members by userId: req.user.id AND associationId, prevents cross-user data leakage. Returns 404 with clear message if no member profile.

routes/exceptional.js line 22-64 (GET /mine): correct — first finds the caller's Member, then includes payments filtered by memberId=member.id. Safe. Note the double authenticateToken (router.use + route-level) at line 22 is redundant but harmless.

routes/auth.js line 106-132: lockout logic is correct — increments failedLoginAttempts on wrong pw, sets lockedUntil=+30min at attempt 5, and resets both on successful login. However, if the user is genuinely locked and then submits a WRONG password again, the code returns 401 immediately without incrementing the counter further AND without updating lockedUntil — this is the desired behavior (lock expires naturally). Good.

routes/auth.js line 106-111: `user.lockedUntil > new Date()` check happens BEFORE bcrypt.compare, so a locked account with wrong credentials will return 403 not 401 — this DOES leak the fact that this specific user exists+is locked (username enumeration via lock state). Acceptable trade-off but note it.

middleware/auth.js line 18-24: loginLimiter max=5 collides with the DB lockout threshold of 5. If a user makes 5 wrong pw attempts, attempt 6 triggers 429 (IP) instead of 403 (account locked). The DB-lock message is only visible from a fresh IP. Raise loginLimiter to 10-15 for cleaner UX.
routes/platform.js line 79-104: same lockout pattern for SUPER_ADMIN — correct and consistent with auth.js.

routes/exceptional.js POST /:id/payments (line 546): admin can post an exceptional payment but there's NO cap check preventing the same member from being paid twice for the same contribution — a duplicate payment would be recorded. Consider a unique (contributionId, memberId) constraint or an explicit dedup check if that's the intended UX.

success_rate.backend: 100% (10/10 pytest cases pass — auth-required checks, admin-without-member 404, admin routes accessible, admin routes protected, lockout after 5 attempts, lock message contains 'bloqué', SuperAdmin password reset unlocks, successful login resets counter)

test_credentials: admin@delete-test.local / admin123 on DELETE-TEST (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md). SuperAdmin drigo@drigo.local / drigo123. Test also creates a throwaway admin test-lockout-<uuid>@delete-test.local for lockout scenarios and cleans up.
seed_data_creation: Throwaway admin user (test-lockout-*) is created in DELETE-TEST for lockout test then deleted via SuperAdmin DELETE /platform/associations/:id/admins/:adminId. No residual test data if teardown ran (verify with GET /platform/associations/{deleteTestId}/admins if in doubt).
context_for_next_testing_agent: The DB lockout test in TestAccountLockout calls `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` twice mid-test to reset the in-memory IP rate-limiter — this is necessary because the loginLimiter (max=5/15min) collides with the DB-lockout threshold (5 attempts). Each backend restart adds ~5s. If the test is run repeatedly, wait ~20s between runs. Existing conftest.py fixtures (admin_client for TEST-NEW-DB assoc) do NOT apply here — this test uses DELETE-TEST association directly per the review request. To run: `cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_kotiz_corrections.py -v`.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — this iteration verifies fixes rather than debugging a new bug. All 5 tested corrections (A, C-backend admin routes, H) behave as specified. The only observation for main agent: the IP-limiter max value (5) collides with the DB lockout threshold (5), so the '403 Compte bloqué' message is masked by the generic '429 Trop de tentatives' from the same IP unless the backend is restarted or 15min pass. This is a UX-only concern, not a functional bug.
